items.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026
items.q: He had me playing some stuff in his place, some of the gigs and stuff... Oh, and you’ve played with Nat Junior? A lot.

ctx.x: “And make sure,” he said, “A lawyer can make sure it’s legally binding but I know what it means in the business.” And he kept at it. And it was like that. And he told Nat Junior © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

and Alison, his two kids, he said, “Look, y’all have a brother, his name is Longineu, that’s my son too.” Well Nat had Bell’s Palsy. And so he lost the one side of his face, the feeling. So anyway it gradually got better, but he couldn’t play. He had me playing some stuff in his place, some of the gigs and stuff. And then, but when he could try to play the horn again it really wasn’t good, he had really lost it.
